subject: Stage 1: zero of ten families survive, control-validated - and your section 7 stop does not reproduce (0.36 fires on 90.7%, not 30%)
body:
Stage 1 has run. Zero of ten families survive. That is the document's expected outcome,
and I checked it before believing it.

THE COUNTS FIRST, as your RULE 4.1 demands. 111,548 bars fingerprinted, 89,238 of them train, 81,851
runs with a direction, and 3,410 EFFECTIVE runs once overlapping runs are counted as fractions -
just above your 3,000 floor. Unconditional mean R is -0.0012.

THE RESULT. Every one of the ten families came in under a correlation of 0.012 against a bar of
2.54. The largest was session at 0.0118. Nothing close.

I DID NOT TRUST THE ZERO ON ITS OWN. Your FP-49 says a pass rate above one in ten means a guard is
broken. A rate of zero deserves the same suspicion - it can equally mean the measurement cannot
detect anything at all. So I planted effects of known strength and re-measured. A planted 0.05 came
back as 0.0499 and cleared the bar; a planted 0.02 came back as 0.0198 and correctly did not; a
planted zero returned zero. The chain recovers what is put into it, so the negative is about the
market and not the instrument.

THE HONEST LIMIT. The smallest effect this design can see at 3,410 runs is 0.0435. You place real
effects at 0.02 to 0.06, so this negative is clean for the upper half of that range and SILENT on
the lower half. An effect at 0.02 or 0.03 is not ruled out and cannot be - your own table needs
12,700 runs for 0.03. I could reach about 11,100 by pooling EURUSD and GBPUSD, but FP-16 treats
other markets as a recurrence test rather than extra sample, so that answers a different question
and I am not doing it quietly.

YOUR SECTION 7 STOP DOES NOT REPRODUCE. You give the stop as 0.36 of typical move and describe it
as firing on about 30% of stops. Read as 0.36 x ATR(14) on USDJPY M5, it fires on 90.7%. The
multiple that actually gives 30% here is 3.42 x ATR - about nine times the stated figure. Your
RULE 7.4 predicted this precisely: the multiple is robust, the inputs are assumed, measure them
before wiring distances. So I implemented the property you described rather than the number, and
recorded 0.36 as not reproducing here rather than silently swapping it.

Your RULE 6.4 formula, on the other hand, reproduces your worked table exactly - all four rows.

ONE LIMITATION I AM NOT HIDING: the outcome's direction is the sign of the agreement score, which is
also one of the ten families. That entangles two of the ten with the outcome they are tested
against. It does not affect the other eight, but you should know it is there.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. This is evidence about ENTRY conditions, on one instrument, at one horizon.
It says nothing about exits - and your RULE 12.1 says the exit is the problem, because run 5
realised 0.50R against a tightest target of 1.27R. I am not calling the edge decision on this.

All ten families are now closed permanently per your RULE 3.2, and Stages 2 and 3 are not reached
because there are no survivors to split. Next is the exit search.
